sentences.text: Eoneustes means "dawn swimmer" and refers to an extinct genus of metriorhynchoid crocodyliform.

The holotype of E. bathonicus was found in Calvados, Normandy, but was lost during the Second World War. E. gaudryi is known from a partial skull holotype found in Côte d’Or, Burgundy, and another partial skull from Alpes-de-Haute-Provence. The genus Eoneustes was described by Young et al. in 2010. The species E. bathonicus was originally described by Mercier in 1933 as Metriorhynchus, and E. gaudryi was originally described by Collot in 1905 as Teleidosaurus.

This animal belonged to the thalattosuchian group, which included species fully adapted to ocean life. It does not belong to either the Teleosauridae or Metriorhynchidae families but is a basal genus related to Metriorhynchidae and the primitive thalattosuchian Teleidosaurus. Eoneustes is classified within the unranked order Mesoeucrocodylia and belongs to the superfamily Metriorhynchoidea.

Eoneustes lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically from the late Bajocian to early Bathonian stages. This corresponds to a time between 168.2 and 165.3 million years ago during the Bathonian stage.
